On one hand, this allows you to check out DLC if your friend/anyone on a public server is hosting a DLC reserve. 

On the other hand. As of time of writing this review, it is 109 GB. Red Dead Redemption 2 is 118 GB. HOW IN THE NAME OF HELL IS THIS GAME ONLY 9 GB LESS THAN RDR2? This game forces you to download every damn unoptimized DLC, and its just making it bloat more and more no matter how much I do not want to buy these damn guns or feeders.

If you have a ton of storage on your PC to burn? Hell, go for it, play the game. But wait for sales and use your money wisely, because there is so much DLC here that you can drain your coffers fast if you're not careful. Saw someone else say the game is ~310$ if you're paying full price for all the current DLC.

If you're like me and don't have 109 GBs to spare to a game that just keeps bloating, do not buy this game.

Benim için sakin ve huzurlu bir şekilde ormanda dolaşıp kafa dağıttığım bir oyun gibi başladı. Köpeğimle birlikte iz sürerek, bazen yürüyerek bazen koşarak haritada gezmek bile başlı başına keyif veriyor. Oyun dışarıdan bakınca “rahat avcılık simülasyonu” gibi duruyor ama işin içine girince olayın ciddiyeti hemen anlaşılıyor.

Özellikle atış kısmı sandığımdan çok daha zor. Scope kullanmadan 50-100-150 metre gibi mesafelerden pompalı ile atış yapmak gerçekten ayrı bir seviye. CS oynayanlar “aimim iyi” diye girerse burada işin sadece aim olmadığını anlıyorlar. Çünkü burada mesafe, mermi düşüşü, rüzgâr ve hayvanın hareketi gibi birçok şey aynı anda devreye giriyor. Yani tek atış ya her şeyi çözüyor ya da tamamen kaçırıyorsun :D

Oyunun en güzel tarafı aslında bu denge. Bir yanda tamamen sakin orman yürüyüşü, diğer yanda tek bir atışta her şeyin değiştiği o gerilim anı. Tutturunca aşırı tatmin ediyor, tutturamayınca da insanın “ben nerede hata yaptım” diye düşünmesine sebep oluyor.

Genel olarak benim için hem kafa boşaltmalık hem de sabır ve dikkat isteyen bir avcılık deneyimi.

My views on this game are mostly neutral, but leaning more towards positive. Let me start off with this game has an absolute crazy amount of content for $20. This game has I think 18 maps (only 2 are free but you can play the other ones), many different species, lots of different weapons, and much more. But man a lot of content is locked behind a paywall. You want a rifle that can hit class 1 animals? You need to pay. You want a blind to hide in? You need to pay. You want new weapons? You need to pay. You want an electronic lure? You need to pay. You want ANYTHING related to an animal on one of the paid maps? You need to pay. You want a new map? You need to pay. Let me say one thing, if you completely ignore ALL the paid stuff and didn't know it was there, it's well worth the money. It still is for how much content you get, but I would rather the game just be $60 and give half the DLCs. They even made it to where you can join multiplayer servers on maps you don't own, as long as someone in the server owns it. But man, it is so annoying that my only options to get class 1 animals with the correct ammo type is a bow or a shotgun, both of which are close range. This game is really worth it, but it leaves a sour taste in your mouth with how much features that should be included in the base game but are locked behind a DLC.

TheHunter: Call of the Wild delivers a one-of-a-kind relaxing wilderness experience.
The visuals and soundscape are phenomenal: rustling leaves, flowing streams, distant bird cries, and dynamic weather turn every map into a living, breathing nature reserve. Animals follow real daily routines—they drink, feed, rest, and flee from noise or foreign scents. Hunting isn’t just point-and-shoot; you must study wind, use calls, pick proper ammo, and stay concealed. Stalking a deer for 40 minutes only to land a clean heart-lung shot gives a rush no action game can replicate.
Multiplayer works smoothly to hunt alongside buddies, and constant free updates add new missions and quality tweaks.
That said, the game has clear flaws. The base game lacks convenient gear like vehicles or tracking dogs, all sold as separate DLC. Progression is slow for new players, and the tutorial barely explains core mechanics like scent zones. If you crave instant gratification or quick gameplay loops, you’ll get bored fast.
But if you enjoy slow, meditative outdoor exploration and deep hunting simulation, ignore the minor downsides. This is the ultimate virtual nature escape worth every penny, especially during sales.

O jogo é uma ótima porta de entrada para jogadores casuais que ainda não estão totalmente ambientados aos simuladores de caça. Os gráficos são excelentes, e a ambientação dos cenários, aliada ao cuidado com a geografia e a cultura local dos países representados, é digna de elogios. Em muitos momentos, chega a ser prazeroso simplesmente caminhar pelo mapa e contemplar os cenários criados. A oferta de armas e equipamentos também é satisfatória. Há uma boa variedade de rifles, miras com visão noturna, alimentadores, estruturas para caça em árvores, equipamentos de camping e até cães de caça com habilidades específicas para diferentes tipos de caçada.

Porém, nem tudo são flores. Embora eu tenha poucas horas registradas na plataforma Steam, acumulei mais de 600 horas no console e sinto que, a cada atualização, o jogo se afasta da simulação e se aproxima de uma experiência mais arcade. O comportamento dos animais tornou-se excessivamente previsível, e a maioria das espécies acaba limitada aos horários de bebida, facilitando o famoso “grind“ em busca de troféus raros. Isso nos leva àquele que considero um dos maiores problemas do jogo: a criação dos Great Ones. Trata-se de animais de nível 10, com aparência única e elevado prestígio. A ideia teve uma boa introdução com o cervo de cauda branca e sua galhada atípica, mas, com o passar do tempo, os visuais adotados tornaram-se cada vez mais exagerados. Hoje encontramos desde gamos com aparências que lembram cervídeos pré-históricos até espécies proibidas para a caça real, como a onça-pintada, exibindo pelagens e padrões inexistentes na natureza. O que deveria representar um verdadeiro “chefão” do mapa, raro e plausível dentro do contexto da fauna local, tornou-se algo cada vez mais fantasioso e irrealista, parecendo ter saído diretamente de um filme de fantasia para dentro do jogo.

No geral, TheHunter: Call of the Wild é um bom jogo, mas um simulador de caça apenas mediano. Mesmo com todos os avanços técnicos e de conteúdo, ele fica devendo em aspectos fundamentais da simulação quando comparado ao seu predecessor, TheHunter Classic, lançado em 2009.

The graphics and sound design are outstanding. Sometimes I just walk through the forests and enjoy the scenery. The multiplayer mode is also fun because hunting with friends creates some unforgettable moments.

Overall, I would definitely recommend The Hunter: Call of the Wild. It has a steep learning curve at first, but once you get used to it, it's an amazing experience. I'd give it a solid **9/10**.

I'm hooked. 
Hunting (sort of) realistically is what I was after.
Accurate animal and hunter behavior. Real physics. Real weapons. That kind of stuff.
"Icarus" and "The Long Dark" cater to those itches but the wild life is all sci-fi.

I've spent time learning many facets of hunting:
... The different ammunitions and how they work with all the different weapons.
... How to reduce my visibility.
... My scent and how that affects my visibility.
... How to somewhat track an animal.
... Where the larger animals' internal organs are located.
... The art of, "calling" the hunted animal which I would need to master for real hunting.
... What it's like to hunt with a hunting dog and why even have one.

Graphics not as good as Dune Awakening, Icarus, or Flight Simulator
Good enough to make "immersion" work though. 

Weather? Light rain and snow that does reduce your visibility to the animals.
Hunker down storms and ray traced footprints in the mud would be nice. But all that stuff would probably need a new engine. Later maybe when they have a billion dollar budget.

All in all a well rounded relaxing hunting game that teaches me a little bit about hunting.
Everything I bought should keep me busy and happy for at least a year.

Well  gotta go now. The jaguar is waiting for his dinner.
Cheers.

I bought this game expecting a hunting experience that would be enjoyable and rewarding, but after a few hours I realized it simply wasn't fun for me.
The biggest issue is the gameplay loop. Most of the time I was walking, tracking footprints, following blood trails, and searching for animals. When I finally found something and took a shot, the animal often ran a huge distance, forcing me to spend even more time tracking it. Instead of feeling exciting, the hunting quickly became repetitive and frustrating.
The game is also far less beginner-friendly than I expected. Animals are extremely sensitive and can disappear before you even get a proper shot. The starting scopes feel underwhelming, ammunition is expensive for new players, and DLC weapons still require purchasing ammo separately, which was disappointing.
Another issue is that opening menus does not properly pause the game. In a single-player hunting game I expected to be able to stop and manage equipment without worrying about the world continuing around me.
During my playtime I spent far more time walking than actually hunting. Tracking wounded animals could take a very long time, and losing an animal after spending several minutes following tracks felt more frustrating than rewarding.
The scenery is beautiful and the Bloodhound DLC is probably the feature I enjoyed most. However, good graphics alone could not make up for gameplay that felt slow, tedious, and overly time-consuming.
I can see why hardcore hunting simulation fans enjoy this game, but for me it was more work than entertainment. I wanted to hunt animals, not spend most of my session walking through the wilderness looking for them.

I genuinely enjoy this game and often come back to it when I want to relax. Coming from fast-paced FPS games like Counter-Strike, this is a refreshing change of pace. The atmosphere, sound design, and attention to detail make the experience feel immersive and rewarding, even during the quieter moments.

My biggest issue with the game is that we're limited to only two reserves unless we purchase additional content. I also feel that a vehicle, such as the quad bike, should be included in the base game. Travelling long distances on foot can become tedious, and even something as simple as a bicycle would make getting around much more enjoyable.

That said, I appreciate that this isn't a game where you can simply run around and shoot every animal you see. It rewards patience, learning the mechanics, understanding animal behaviour, and carefully planning your hunts. The progression can be slow, but that's part of what makes each successful hunt feel satisfying.

I would highly recommend this game, especially if it included the quad bike and a few additional reserves to provide more variety in terms of animals and hunting locations. Aside from those points, the game is honestly fantastic and one of the most relaxing hunting experiences I've played.

No, the reason I don't recommend this game is because huge amounts of pretty basic content are locked behind DLC. Want an ATV to traverse these huge maps faster? Want the ability to choose where to put blinds or tents? Want to set up tree stands or have a hunting dog to retrieve birds or track your prey? Want to just, like, customize your guns with anything other than like... 4 basic colors and a tiny number of camo patterns? All paid DLC.

Oh, and those tents? They're fully functional outposts that let you access your storage as well as buy new guns, ammo, and equipment from the store, as well as summon your ATV to the tent's location. All of this in a tent that you can just carry with you and plop down whenever you want and then pick right back up as you please. What's the point of using a backpack for 3 to 9 extra pounds of inventory space when you can just carry your entire storage with you WITHOUT the extra visibility and noise caused by the backpacks? I know it's not a competitive game but that's still pretty busted, especially for paid DLC.

Oyun çok güzel. Hayvanların gerçekçiliği ve kalitesi inanılmaz iyi. Atmosfer de gerçekten av yaptığınızı hissettiriyor diyebilirim. Oyunda birçok farklı hayvan türü, harita, silah, dürbün ve çağırıcılar gibi ekipmanlar bulunuyor. Hayvan avlama mekaniği de efsane ötesi.

Oyuna ilk girdiğinizde sistemi hemen öğrenemeyebilirsiniz. Ben ilk başladığımda hiçbir hayvanı vurmayı bırak, görememiştim bile. Ancak birkaç saat oynayıp mekaniği çözdükten sonra oyun gerçekten eğlenceli hale geliyor ve hızlı bir şekilde avlanmaya başlayabiliyorsunuz.

Ama şunu özellikle söylemeliyim: kesinlikle oyunun yanında köpek DLC’sini almanız şart. Yoksa vurduğunuz hayvanın izini saatlerce ararsınız ya da hiç bulamazsınız. Bu DLC oyun deneyimini ciddi şekilde kolaylaştırıp eğlenceli bir hale getiriyor.

Oyun başlangıçta 2 harita ile geliyor. Bu haritalar sizi bir süre fazlasıyla idare eder, çünkü oyun yavaş tempolu ilerlediği için içerik açısından sıkıntı yaşatmıyor. Ancak aslan gibi daha farklı hayvan türlerini avlamak istiyorsanız, DLC olarak sunulan birçok farklı harita da mevcut.

Önemli:
Bu oyun tamamen gerçekçilik üzerine kurulmuş bir avcılık simülasyonudur. Oyunda rastgele koşamazsınız, hızlı gidemezsiniz veya acele edemezsiniz. Oyunu gerçekçi yapan en önemli şeylerden biri de budur. Oyun oldukça yavaş ilerler, bu yüzden bu tarz şeyleri sevmiyorsanız kesinlikle uzak durmanız gereken bir yapım.

Ayrıca Epic Games’te hem oyunun kendisi hem de DLC’leri Steam’e kıyasla çok daha uygun fiyatlı. Oraya da göz atabilirsiniz.

This is a tentative yes. I don't think this game is for everyone.
I picked it up on special because it seemed interesting. 
Very nice looking, I grabbed the Emerald Coast because that's where I live and there are some places that really seem familiar I think I know where they got the inspiration.
The animals are very well detailed and responsive, to the point where stalking a beast can be quite tricky. Movement is painfully slow if you want to be quiet and it takes a while to work out the rhythm of movement in order to get close to animals, especially if you are trying to master bow hunting. 

I have been amazed how animals can trick you into losing their trail by doubling back on you.

The ATV DLC is essential, and it is a bit rude that they made it a DLC in my opinion. The maps are enormous and if you wanted to walk everywhere to unlock shelters it would be incredibly long and arduously boring. 
All the other DLC are optional, you can have a good experience without any of it. 

I suggest not paying too much attention to the missions, they are *kind of* stupid. Just immerse yourself in stalking, or ambushing (if thats your thing) and getting clean kills and upgrading your stats. 

All in all I would say it's quite a nice game, I find it very relaxing and the scenery is spectacular. 
It also runs quite well on my old machine on ultra everything, which is also a bonus. 
Pick it up if you like slow burns, and taking your time. If you want run and gun fast paced action I would give it a miss.

TL;DR - Buy only if you're fine with buying a lot of DLC and don't care about your data being harvested.

The good:
- This game is one of the best (if not the best) in its genre. If not for the negatives I described below, it would easily be a very enjoyable comfort game I could play and revisit for a looong time. Likely would have Overwhelmingly Positive for its Steam user rating, too.
- You can play this game as a walking simulator. Play YouTube videos or watch TV on your second screen and just... Relax. Explore nature without urgent objectives or "exciting" time limits.
- There's multiplayer support. This is a big plus. Even though whoever is more skilled is better off hunting alone, just having an option of playing together contributes to fun.

The bad:
- The game is not nearly as enjoyable without the DLCs. Most of the content and usable equipment is locked behind extra cash. The 20€ game is a very limited Demo version. Even some QoL features are sold as DLCs.
- You can't make any animals friendly to you or even used to you. They all act very mechanically. You're a hunter. Period.
- You can't climb. Feels like any slope steeper than 45° is impassable terrain.
- Animals have infinite stamina. You can keep scaring them and they keep running forever. They never tire. You can't try persistence hunting in this game.

The ugly:
- Other than a separate EULA, the game has its own, very invasive, Privacy Policy. If you live where GDPR applies, you may opt out by sending them an e-mail. I had sent that e-mail, but got not reply in return. No idea if it worked.
- There are many immersion-breaking things. Not big negatives, but it does keep reminding you that it's a game. A somewhat unpolished digital product. Here are some examples (there are more, though):
--- While riding a quad, I often "heard" rabbits thumping threateningly... From over 300m away. 
--- There are some floating rocks and tree trunks. 
--- You can clip through some objects (mostly rocks).
--- Some light sources appear and disappear depending on where you're looking.
--- Animals can sometimes run, turn 170° on a dime, run back for a second and make the same turn again.
- Once you figure out how AI behaves, you can optimize the fun out of the game, much like playing tic-tac-toe.
- Tracks are visible on dirt, but if the dirt is covered in gravel or grass, you have to rely on holograms. It would be ideal if the game were playable without holograms, even if it meant less convenience.

A lifetime of digital warfare. XIII 2v2s on Xfire. Frontlines of MoH:AA. Gravity Guns of HL2. Instagibbing in Quake 3. Slide-cancelling in Warzone. Premier elite in CS2.

Now? Neurons fried. Reflexes gone. So I swapped full-auto for one clean breath.

No spawn traps. No sweats. Just wind through pines, leaves under boots, and a moose that owes me nothing. I track him for hours, across ridges and riverbeds. I watch him drink. I watch him feed. I listen to his mating calls.

Then, finally, at the anatomically right angle, I raise my rifle. Right there, he looks me straight in the eye. Direct contact. He looks at me—not with fear, not with rage. Just... recognition. Like he knew I'd miss. [b] Like he'd been waiting for me to learn something the hard way [/b].

I focus. Hold my breath. Squeeze the trigger. Not aiming for the head this time—lungs. Like I've done countless times before.

The shot fires. It hits. But not where it needed to.

He stumbles. Shakes his head. Then he charges, tosses me like a ragdoll, hoof to the ribs. I limp away bruised and bleeding, watching him vanish into the treeline. There is a thin trail of blood, I am too weak to go through. But I feel no rage at all, a faint but genuine smile is on my face.

I whistle for my dog to follow. Both my best friend and therapist. He didn't care that I whiffed. Didn't judge when I got tossed. Just wagged, sniffed, and limped beside this old soldier through the quiet woods. That's when it hit: [b] life isn't about the shot. It's about the moments between [/b].

Came for the hunt. Stayed for the peace.

Comprei esse jogo junto com vários outros para um amigo que tinha acabado de montar um computador pela primeira vez e nunca tinha jogado nada. Melhor coisa que eu fiz, já tenho 40h em 5 dias, ele tem algumas a mais. 

GAMEPLAY:
É um SIMULADOR de caça, esse nome não é para se gabar ou fingir que adultos não estão jogando: é para sinalizar que você não vai sair por aí correndo e dando tiro para todo lado. 

O começo é bem difícil, até se acostumar com as características dos animais, com o comportamento e com as fugas, principalmente se não tiver nenhuma expansão. A partir do momento em que você entende o básico (comportamento dos animais, rotina [horário que eles comem, bebem e como eles te identificam] e como se locomover e atirar), o jogo começa a ser um desafio saldável contra sigo mesmo: você quer constantemente achar um animal melhor e acertá-lo de forma mais limpa e mais rápida. 
O jogo é sensacional, cada mapa, cada grind (caçar de forma focada e repetida um animal em específico para conquistar troféus, conquistas ou só por ser uma espécie que você gosta) é diferente e muito interessante.

GASTAR DINHEIRO COM EXPANSÃO:
O jogo tem centenas de dlc's (expansões) e nenhuma delas é obrigatória para você se divertir ou pay-to-win. A começar que você não está competindo com ninguém, o jogo é feito para você passar um tempo e se divertir, mas todas elas adicionam mapas, armas ou ferramentas de caça novas. 

De qualquer forma, acho que é interessante, ao comprar o jogo, comprar algumas expansões para um pontapé inicial:

1 - Um ou dois mapas adicionais: Para você identificar que tipo de bioma gosta mais de caçar
2 - Um ou dois packs de armas: De começo você não vai ter armas que abrangem todas as classes de animais ( que vão de 1 a 9, de acordo com o calibre da munição que você atira, animais minúsculos, como coelhos são 1 e animais gigantes como crocodilos de água salgada são 9). Então eu comprei, e recomendo, o Modern Weapon Pack¹, Weapon Pack 1² e o High Caliber Weapon Pack. Tudo custou pouco menos de R$20,00 e facilitam muito a vida, embora eu pudesse comprar armas que fariam um trabalho semelhante com o avançar do jogo, mas é tudo tão barato.
3 - O que mais você quiser para se divertir. Meu amigo gosta de caçar animais na Savana Africana, eu gosto de caçar aves e veados, cada um de seu jeito.

ASPECTOS DO JOGO:
Gráfico - 9/10
Ambientação - 10/10
Otimização - 10/10
Som - 10/10 (é impressionante)
Facilidade de aprendizado - 08/10 (eu jogo video-game há anos, meu amigo começou agora e ambos estamos nos dando muito bem, vendo um vídeo aqui e lendo um post no reddit ali, mas tudo certo)

Call of the wild is a well crafted, highly immersive outdoor walking simulator. I've found myself watching the sunrise and sunset, I'll walk to a random spot in the woods and bathe in the sights and sounds of the game. Walking through the DLC "Mississippi Acres Preserve" Feels like walking back home. 
Despite how well crafted this game is, I can't recommend it, for two reasons:
    It's incredibly frustrating to play as someone coming into the space from the more generic shooters. Bullet drop, I can account for. Wind throwing off my shot? I can deal with that. It's perfectly reasonable to have realistic ballistics in a game like this. Skill issues aside, this game doesn't just fight you every time you raise your rifle, it kicks your teeth in. For fun, I went to a crouching position, took aim at a tree about a hundred yards away, and just watched. My sights drifted dozens of yards to the left, came back to center, and drifted dozens of yards to the left again. There's some kind of feedback pulling your sights away from whatever direction you're trying to go. Holding your breath doesn't have a profound effect on your character either. Prone offers zero relief. There's a skill tree that I'm not far into that I'm certain corrects this but it's unreasonable to start THIS bad.  
    I wasn't joking about this being a walking simulator. It takes forever to get anywhere in this game. The maps are massive, which is good! Why does it bother me so much? The devs gave us a solution in the form of DLC!  ATV SABER 4X4 is paywalled and it is a NEED in this game. It can take hours to walk to points of interest. Why they added a 4x4 as a DLC I'll never know. (It's obvious) 
    They've made an amazing game but they've also made decisions questionable enough to prevent me from recommending this game. I'm going to keep playing, but I wont be happy about it.

《猎人：荒野的召唤》：在快时代里，做一场关于耐心的梦
2017年2月16日，当Expansive Worlds将《猎人：荒野的召唤》推向世界时，几乎没有人能预料到，这款节奏慢到近乎反商业的狩猎模拟游戏，会在接下来的近十年间俘获数百万玩家的心。Steam平台近14万条评价中88%的好评率，全球预估销量突破1380万份，以及持续至今的DLC更新——这些数字背后是一个耐人寻味的事实：在一个追求“快”的时代，一款逼迫你“慢”下来的游戏，反而成了无数人心中无法替代的港湾。

99%的时间，不在扳机上
《猎人：荒野的召唤》最反常规的地方在于：它几乎不算一款射击游戏。

有玩家统计过，单次完整狩猎平均耗时3小时17分钟，其中追踪与潜行占2小时52分钟，开枪决策仅占8分钟，从击中到回收猎物不过7分钟。99%的时间，你都在做一件事——等待。等待风停，等待猎物靠近，等待那个千载难逢的瞬间。

但这份等待绝非无所事事。你需要根据动物的足迹、气味、声音等蛛丝马迹来判断它的行踪和位置。一只白尾鹿从发现脚印到最终放倒，需交叉验证3类粪便温度、4处蹄印朝向、2次叫声方位提示及实时风向偏移值。风向影响气味扩散，心率影响瞄准稳定性，弹道需手动计算下坠——射击前的准备，比扣动扳机本身耗费十倍的心神。

游戏中的62种动物均按真实生物节律活动：驼鹿每日18:30准时抵达湖岸饮水；松鸡清晨5:20至6:10在林缘草甸集群觅食。它们不是随机刷新的靶子，而是有作息、有领地、有习性的生态演员。正如一位评测者所说：“你真正对抗的，从来不是猎物，而是自己的急躁”。

一个会呼吸的开放世界
如果说狩猎系统是《猎人：荒野的召唤》的骨骼，那么它的开放世界就是灵魂。

游戏提供了多个根据现实设计的狩猎区域，地形、物种、气候都贴合真实。从北美密林到非洲草原，从欧洲湿地到西伯利亚冻原——每一个保护区都是一幅可以步入的风景画。

画面虽保留着2017年的技术水准，却依然令人叹服：分层云朵缓缓移动，动态落叶随风飘落，水面波纹由实时风速驱动，反射天空云层移动速度与实拍气象数据误差小于0.3秒/分钟。有玩家评价道：“风景是真好啊”；另一位则直言自己是来玩“步行旅游模拟器”的。天气变化与昼夜交替不仅是视觉点缀，更是狩猎中必须考量的外在环境——晨雾的透光率每5分钟更新一次，直接影响瞄准镜的视野通透度。

在这个世界里，你不再是一个“玩家”，你只是一个在荒野中穿行的人。

当耐心成为一种稀缺品
《猎人：荒野的召唤》对耐心的要求，几乎是“劝退级别”的。

新手两小时绕圈找不到猎物是常态。有豆瓣玩家吐槽：“我新手一进游戏就走错了方向，然后在林子里逛了两小时连根毛都没打到”。有人称它为“跑步模拟器”，有人说“适合巨闲的人，心急的玩不了”。

但正是这种“劝退”，筛选出了真正愿意沉浸其中的玩家。Metacritic上一位用户写道：“Very fun once you get good at it it was slow at first”——上手之后非常有趣，只是开头慢而已。另一位豆瓣玩家说：“从散步模拟器到第一个钻石，到第一个异色，再到第一个珍惜驼鹿。真·养老游戏”。

游戏的“道德狩猎系统”进一步强化了这种克制的美学。使用不当武器猎杀小型动物会被判定为“过度杀伤”，仅发放32%的基础经验与青铜奖牌；而用匹配的武器完成一击毙命，则可获得100%经验与钻石奖牌。连续两枪未致命，动物逃逸后30分钟内无法再次标记，当日所有狩猎收益减半。这套机制不是在教你“怎么杀”，而是在教你“为什么杀”以及“如何尊重生命”。

永不落幕的旅程
《猎人：荒野的召唤》的另一大魅力，在于它从未停止生长。

游戏发售至今，Expansive Worlds持续推出了数十款DLC——新地图、新武器、新物种、新伙伴。玩家可以和好友组成最多八人的狩猎小队，分工配合，享受合作狩猎的乐趣。游戏本体在促销时价格极低，性价比极高。有玩家在Metacritic上写道：“been playing since 2019 and never gets boring”——从2019年玩到现在，从未厌倦。

而游戏社区的氛围同样令人称道。一位Metacritic用户评价道：“The game has an amazing community on discord with no toxicity”——社区氛围极好，毫无 toxicity。在这个充满戾气的网络时代，一个能让人静下心来交流的玩家群体，本身就是一种稀缺的馈赠。

结语
《猎人：荒野的召唤》不是一款适合所有人的游戏。它慢、它难、它不讨好。它用近乎严苛的拟真，把虚拟狩猎变成一种具身认知训练——在等待中学会观察，在克制中理解平衡，在收获时体会敬畏。

但它恰恰是这个快时代里最稀缺的那种游戏。当短视频把我们的注意力切成碎片，当3A大作恨不得每三秒给你一个高光时刻——《猎人：荒野的召唤》选择了一条截然相反的路。它要求你放下手机，关掉音乐，戴上耳机，在虚拟的荒野中静静等待。等待风把气味吹向正确的方向，等待那只鹿从树影中走出，等待你的呼吸与瞄准镜中的十字线合二为一。

它不是射击游戏，而是一场持续数小时的自然观察实验。它让你在一次次空手而归中学会耐心，在一次次精准命中中收获敬畏。它用1380万份销量和88%的好评率证明了一件事：在这个浮躁的世界里，依然有无数人渴望一场安静的、漫长的、与自己对话的旅程。

如果你愿意慢下来——那么，背上你的猎枪，走进那片荒野吧。风在等你，鹿在等你，而你自己，也在等你。

História: Vou considerar a história do mapa Layton Lake para essa rewiew. A história é bem simples, envolve algumas atividades rotineiras no manejo de animais em uma reserva de caça e trilhas, você é solicitado pelos trabalhadores do parque para fazer alguns serviços, como caçar animais, fotografar, ajudar na procura de pessoas perdidas, etc... Parece bem simples e realmente é, mas por incrível que pareça, é bem legal, os personagens são legais, as missões são de maioria interessantes e pelo menos para mim gerou um incentivo ainda maior para jogar o jogo, eu sei que muitos ignoram as missões ou fazem elas sem prestar atenção, mas eu recomendo dar pelo menos uma lida na legenda, vale a pena. 

Gameplay: Esse jogo te ensina na força a ter paciência, eu sei que cotw não é o simulador de caça mais realista do mercado, mas até você aprender como os animais funcionam e como agem, você precisa ter paciência e cautela, acho isso muito legal desse jogo, em meio a tantos jogos que tentam ser o mais rápidos e poluídos de informação, the hunter faz o contrario, te forçando a ter calma e aprender com os erros nas caçadas, é meio besta mas the hunter é um ótimo jogo para reduzir o estresse e a ansiedade, caso você esteja 100& focado nele.
Um ponto que acho bem negativo no quesito da gameplay, é a baixa quantidade de armas que possuímos no jogo base, com uma grande parte sendo desbloqueada apenas via dlcs, você tem tudo que precisa no jogo base, mas acaba ficando com pouca variedade, pelo menos as dlcs são baratas. 

Gráficos: Joguei em uma 4060 com ryzen 5 500, joguei no máximo em full hd. É bizarro o quanto esse jogo é bonito e tecnicamente leve, a todo momento que você anda pelo mapa você encontra um cenário que seria facilmente uma área de trabalho de windons 7, se possível, jogue com os gráficos no ultra ou alto, você não vai se arrepender.

The character glides effortlessly across brutal terrain, can sprint for miles without slowing down, and if they stop for a second, they can still nail an animal from a ridiculous distance despite sounding like they've just finished a marathon.

But walking up a hill? Apparently that's completely bloody impossible. Absolutely ridiculous.

This character is practically overqualified for every other physical task in the game, but a slight incline? Nope. That's where we draw the line. The daft bastard looks like they ought to be able to climb trees if they felt like it, yet a grassy slope is somehow their greatest nemesis. Honestly... it's absurd.

It ruins the experience far more than it should. Instead of simply walking up a bank, you're forced to bunny-hop your way to the top. By the time you've finished, you've scared every animal within a ten-mile radius. Probably a few in the next county as well.

Another feature that really ought to disappear is animals floating away in the water. The idea makes sense if you've shot something a few metres offshore. Fair enough.

But if I shoot a massive bull moose eight metres up the bloody riverbank, it should not suddenly decide it's a canoe and drift off downstream. That's just not how physics works. That's embarrassing, ♥♥♥♥♥♥' hell

I'm a noob to the hunting game genre, but I saw this on a deep sale last Christmas and decided to just go ahead and buy it. I did not expect to be as hooked as I was! This game is great fun, and an excellent thing to play while chatting on a call, listening to Youtube or a podcast, or even just quietly as you immerse yourself running through the beautiful landscapes. The beginning two maps are HUGE, with plenty of landmarks to examine and explore. I spent 40 hours on Hirschfelden and Leyton Lakes before even bothering to check out any other maps, and even now I've only barely dipped my toes in Medved-Taiga. There's so much to do and explore!

The hunting itself definitely had a bit of a learning curve for a beginner not familiar with the genre (like me). While I WAS able to bring down game, often I would shoot and not secure a kill and track it across half the map (not fun), or I'd secure the kill but get a poor rating. After doing a little googling and practicing a bit, though, I started getting those nice one-shot kills and can now even manage to hit heart shots for maximum quick kill bonus. I'm definitely still in the earlier stages (I have yet to get a diamond harvest), but now that I have some experience under my belt it's great fun trying to maximize my points and kill my targets with the most accurate and efficient shots as possible. I can't wait to slowly play my way across all of these beautiful and varied maps!

One thing I will say though, the dog DLC is definitely an early necessity in order to help with tracking. Once you get better at dropping the animal in a single shot the dog doesn't help as much, but early on I found it indispensable, especially since it can track blood that you the player cannot see. A lot of people also consider the ATVs to be necessary, but in my opinion I actually spend most of my time on foot and rarely use them, at least right now. I can see them becoming more useful once you've explored more of the map and want to get to specific hunting areas. Overall, I do recommend buying the Starter Bundle Pack if you're going to get into this game, just for some of the perk items it allows you access to.

I love the immersion offered by The Hunter: Call of the Wild, especially those quiet moments between hunts. However, I feel that the map's structures, like the outposts and lookouts, lack a bit of life and interactivity.
It would be fantastic if they added small mechanics to enhance the role-playing and realism within these locations. For example, the benches at the lookouts or the chairs inside the outposts could be more than just decorative; you could actually sit on them to rest while enjoying the views or waiting for the weather to change. Then you could use the stoves or campfires at the outposts to cook something basic with what you've gathered (or simply as an animation/function to pass the time), which would give much more purpose and meaning to returning to the shelter.
These are small interaction details that don't affect the main hunting loop, but they would make the world feel much more alive and welcoming during breaks.

Do not buy this if you plan to play co-op. The developers heavily prioritize pumping out paid DLC maps and gear packs over fixing core gameplay mechanics that have been broken for years. They are entirely focused on extracting revenue rather than improving quality of life. Major issues my wife and I constantly face in multiplayer: Game-Breaking Audio Desync: Clicking on an empty chamber triggers a full-volume gunfire blast on the other player's screen. This "ghost shot" completely ruins co-op coordination and instantly spooks all animals within 250+ meters. Busted Dog Audio: The companion Bloodhound's directional audio is completely broken, constantly locking to the left audio channel even when the dog is on your right. Broken Stealth Mechanics: Animal detection is incredibly punishing. Moving at a normal walk (3 white bars) spooks animals instantly because the game's noise meter lies and doesn't accurately calculate brush movement. Useless Perks & No Water Traversal: The perk system is a joke, offering barely noticeable 5% stat changes that do not affect gameplay. There is also zero water traversal, forcing you into massive detours around tiny streams. The core hunting loop can be fun, but the developers' refusal to fix game-breaking multiplayer bugs while demanding more money for DLC makes it impossible to recommend.

《荒野之呼》，原野狩猎之佳制，复刻五洲荒林野泽，尽展天地原生之貌。山川绵延，草木疏密随地而异，溪涧流泉，风过林梢皆有实声，朝暮晨昏光影流转，晴雾雨雪四时变幻，鸟兽栖行皆循天性，无矫揉造作之态。
境内百余种走兽飞禽，麋鹿孤狼、野猪野禽，各有习性，辨足迹、闻啼鸣、观粪便，方能寻其踪迹。猎具品类周全，长短枪械、弓弩、诱鸣哨、气味诱饵各司其职，需屏息缓行，逆风潜近，一击方得成效。不可肆意乱射，惊扰群兽，狩猎之道重在静与察，非恃蛮力。
地域广远，欧陆丛林、北美荒原、非洲草原、澳洲郊野，地貌生灵各不相同。可独游山野，循迹寻猎；亦可与同好结伴同驰，共探深林，分寻兽群，共享猎获。每擒异兽，可录图鉴，记其身形、栖息之所，日积月累，渐晓百兽之性。
然亦有缺憾。独行久则景致相近，奔走赶路耗时颇多，代步之器寥寥。兽类 AI 心智浅薄，偶有举止违和。枪械手感偏柔，中弹判定时有参差。地图广袤，无便捷速传之法，往返跋涉易生倦怠。原生内容有限，诸多珍兽、新境皆需另购拓展。
统而论之，此作弃喧嚣杀伐，独取山野静趣，光影音效写实至极，潜心观兽寻踪者，自得悠然之乐。若喜静心远足、偏爱写实狩猎，实为良选；若嗜快节奏激战、厌长途跋涉，则难称心意。写实猎游之中，鲜有能及此作气韵者。
TheHunter: Call of the Wild is an excellent work of wild hunting, recreating forests and marshes across five continents, showing the true appearance of untamed nature. Mountains stretch far, plants grow thick or thin with the land; brooks murmur, winds rustle leaves with lifelike sound. Light shifts with dawn and dusk, mist, rain and snow change through seasons, and beasts and fowls move and rest as their nature bids, no artificial falsity to behold.
More than a hundred beasts and birds dwell within its bounds: stags, lone wolves, boars and wild fowl each follow their own ways. Thou trackest them by footprints, cries and droppings to find their haunts. Hunting gear aboundeth: long and short firearms, bows, caller whistles and scent lures serve sundry ends. Thou must creep soft, hold thy breath, draw near against the wind to strike true. Wild shooting scareth all herds away; the art of hunting lieth in calm observation, not brute force.
Its lands stretch wide: European woodlands, North American wastes, African savannas and Australian outbacks each bear unique landforms and creatures. Thou mayst wander the wilds alone, tracking game; or ride forth with companions, rove deep woods side by side, seek herds apart and share thy quarry. Every rare beast thou takest fill thy codex, recording its shape and dwelling place, till thou knowest all wild creatures well.
Yet blemishes remain. After long lone wandering, landscapes grow alike, and much time is spent tramping empty ground with scarce mounts to speed thy way. The beasts’ wit is shallow, their acts oft unnatural. Firearms feel soft, and hit judgment faileth at times. The maps are vast, yet no swift travel ease thy endless treks, breeding weariness. Base game content is thin, most rare beasts and new lands require purchased expansions.
Weigh its worth: it casteth aside noisy combat, and offereth quiet wild delight, with hyper-realistic light and sound. Those who love slow hiking and authentic tracking shall taste pure peace here. If thou seekest fast-paced clashes or hatest long treks, it shall not suit thee. Among all realistic hunting games, few match its serene atmosphere.

Despite being a decade old at this point, theHunter: Call of the Wild still holds up as one of the more thoughtful hunting sims out there, largely because of how it handles pacing and immersion.
Challenges and focus
The Challenges are a real highlight. Tasking you with hunting specific animals using specific weapons narrows your attention in a good way, instead of scanning the whole map for anything that moves, you're locked onto particular target types and behaviours, which makes each session feel more purposeful. It's the difference between wandering and hunting.
Ambience and audio
The ambience is genuinely well done. Once you spend enough time in a zone, you start picking out animal calls and background noise and instinctively knowing what species or activity it signals, without needing to lean on the UI prompts. That's the sim doing its job properly, teaching you to read the environment by ear.
Unfortunately, that's undercut by a recurring bug where animal call audio just doesn't play, replaced by a visual "you heard something" cue instead. It's a frustrating gap because it's exactly the kind of moment the ambience is supposed to reward you for, and instead you get a UI crutch standing in for the real thing. It breaks immersion right when the game's sound design is otherwise doing the heavy lifting.
Graphics and scale
Graphically, it's fair for its age, you're not getting a modern showcase, but it's aged reasonably and the environments carry it well. Where the game really opens up is the DLC map packs. They add substantial, varied terrain and give you a lot of freedom in how you approach a hunt, whether that's stalking, spot and stalk, photography, or straightforward hunting expeditions.
Content and structure
Beyond the core hunting loop, there's a story thread to follow, landmarks scattered across maps worth tracking down, and plenty of room to just wander, spotting animals, photographing them, or taking the shot. It rewards patience over rushing, which suits the sim genre.
Overall
A strong hunting sim let down by an audio bug that undermines its own best feature. The Challenge system and ambient sound design show real design intent, but that intent gets partially wasted when the audio cue system fails to deliver the calls it's meant to.

Title: A Meditative Masterpiece of Patience and Solitude ⭐⭐⭐⭐

theHunter: Call of the Wild isn't a game for everyone—but for those who appreciate silence, patience, and the subtle beauty of nature, it's an absolute treasure.

In a world of fast-paced shooters and hyperactive open worlds, this is something rare: a slow, meditative simulation that values patience over reflexes. You'll spend most of your time creeping through forests, following tracks, droppings, and animal calls, hoping to line up the perfect shot. There's no hand-holding here. The game expects you to understand animal behavior, wind direction, scent carry, and weapon ballistics. It's part simulation, part game—and once you settle into its rhythm, it's incredibly rewarding.

The atmosphere is where Call of the Wild truly excels. Each reserve is a sprawling, hand-crafted environment brimming with stunning detail—misty European forests, sun-drenched African savannahs, snowy taigas, and more. The dynamic weather, full day-night cycles, and incredibly realistic sound design pull you in completely. Birds chirp overhead, distant calls echo through the trees, your footsteps crunch softly beneath you. The graphics are so stunning that you'll find yourself pausing just to take in the view.

The gunplay is satisfying and realistic. Breath control steadies your aim, but running too long makes your heart race and your sights wobble. Every shot requires careful consideration of distance, caliber, and placement. And when that hour-long stalk finally ends in a clean, ethical kill? The payoff is unmatched.

Yes, the learning curve is steep. The pace is glacial. And with over 90% positive reviews on Steam and countless DLCs adding new reserves, weapons, and species, the content is virtually endless. But that's the beauty of it—this is a game to lose yourself in, not to rush through.

If you're looking for a quick adrenaline fix, look elsewhere. But if you find beauty in quietude and satisfaction in a well-placed shot after a long, patient stalk, theHunter: Call of the Wild is a masterclass in immersive simulation. It captures the peace, tension, and thrill of the hunt like no other game on the market.

Not every game has to be loud to be powerful—and Call of the Wild proves it. 🦌🌲🔭

You can upgrade skills and perks as you level up from experience gained by exploring and killing things! Shoot a damn rabbit in the head if you want. The maps are absolutely HUGE and on sale right now (July 9, 2026) I can't find one thing to complain about. I guess if you don't like games where 90% of the time all you hear is nature sounds and the crunch of leaves or snow underfoot, you'll get stir crazy. Otherwise BIG recommend. Oh also if you don't have a really good PC you likely won't be able to appreciate the best the game has to offer in terms of immersion into a beautiful nature reserve. 

Keep in mind, I only have 2.5 hours played and the above is just SCRATCHING the surface. Okay one last thing: you don't have to worry about prone crawling everywhere to avoid snapping the wrong twig and sending every animal in a 100 ft radius to the hills. As long as you aren't hipfiring your shotgun every two seconds you likely will run into deer and other animals without too much effort, but the key is to make sure you hit them or else the gunfire WILL scare them off. No matter - then the chase begins and you can start tracking them!

Травоядные будут возвращаться на место водопоя, кормежки, ночлега после убийства 1-2 сородичей, ведь в игре есть волшебное слово "пресс убийств" ну да животные не могут учуять запахи крови и туш сородичей, но зато они туда не пойдут после 4-5 убийств, у нас же животные могут в карту заглядывать и видеть где эти светло-фиолетовые кругляшки есть да? -"Но есть же хищные животные" и то ей Богу они тут более менее нормальные: койоты и лисы сразу убегут при запахе или при громком звуке. This game is one of the most beautiful and immersive experiences I've played. The environments are stunning, the wildlife feels alive, and every hunt tells its own story. Sometimes you'll spend 20 minutes tracking a single animal, and when you finally get the perfect shot, it feels incredibly rewarding.

What I love most is that the game lets you play at your own pace. You don't have to rush or constantly be in action. You can explore massive maps, enjoy the scenery, listen to nature, and hunt whenever you're ready. It's surprisingly relaxing after a long day.

Why you should play it:

🌲 Beautiful open-world maps with incredible attention to detail.
🦌 Realistic animal behavior that makes every hunt unique.
🎯 Rewarding gameplay where patience and skill pay off.
🤝 Great solo or with friends.
🎧 Amazing sound design that makes the world feel alive.

Even if you've never been interested in hunting, this game is worth trying. It's just as much about exploring nature and enjoying the journey as it is about taking the shot.

If you're looking for a game that's both relaxing and rewarding, theHunter: Call of the Wild is an easy recommendation.

Una de las mayores decepciones que me he llevado con un juego. Menos mal lo compré en oferta y no a precio completo, porque sinceramente esperaba una experiencia mucho más entretenida o, al menos, algo similar al juego para móviles.

Desafortunadamente, este juego tiene una jugabilidad muy pobre y unas mecánicas que rápidamente se vuelven repetitivas y aburridas. Para la experiencia que pretende ofrecer, incluso siento que el apartado gráfico se queda un poco corto.

Lo que terminó de arruinar la experiencia fue el sistema de caza. Es absurdo dispararle a un venado a unos 20 metros, justo donde el propio juego te indica, y que aun así salga corriendo como si nada, obligándote a perseguirlo durante 500 metros hasta que finalmente muere. Para empeorar las cosas, el juego ni siquiera muestra dónde impactó el disparo, por lo que nunca sabes si realmente fallaste o simplemente el juego decidió no registrarlo correctamente. Jamás pensé que la ausencia de una simple kill cam pudiera restarle tanto valor a un juego.

Entiendo que quienes busquen una experiencia más realista puedan disfrutarlo, pero ese supuesto realismo pierde todo el sentido cuando puedes dispararle a un animal en la cabeza y este simplemente huye como si no hubiera pasado nada.

Otro punto muy negativo es el ritmo del juego. Puedes pasar más de 15 minutos recorriendo el mapa sin encontrar un solo animal, y las misiones tampoco ayudan. Al comenzar apenas explican las mecánicas básicas y avanzar en los objetivos se convierte en una odisea: el mapa ofrece muy poca orientación, puedes perder más de una hora buscando una ubicación para que, al llegar, la misión simplemente te envíe a otro punto del mapa sin que ocurra nada interesante.

En definitiva, me parece un juego con una idea muy prometedora, pero con una ejecución que deja mucho que desear. La falta de acción, la repetitividad y algunas decisiones de diseño terminaron haciendo que la experiencia fuera más frustrante que divertida.

Eso sí, queda claro que este no es un juego para todo el mundo. Si disfrutas de simuladores de caza muy pausados y no te importa dedicar largos periodos a explorar sin apenas acción, probablemente puedas sacarle más provecho que yo. En mi caso, terminó siendo una gran decepción.

# TheHunter: Call of the Wild – Simulador de caminhada com participação especial de um animal

Entrei em **TheHunter: Call of the Wild** preparado para viver a experiência definitiva da caça.

Eu seria silencioso.

Paciente.

Preciso.

Uma mistura de caçador profissional, documentarista do Discovery Channel e predador supremo da cadeia alimentar.

Na prática?

Eu virei praticante de caminhada ecológica.

Comecei a partida equipado com rifle, binóculo e uma confiança completamente incompatível com a minha habilidade.

Olhei o mapa.

Marquei um ponto.

E comecei a andar.

Andei por uma hora.

Nada.

Duas horas.

Nada.

Três horas.

Nem um passarinho com problema de autoestima.

A floresta estava completamente vazia.

Não tinha cervo.

Não tinha javali.

Não tinha coelho.

Não tinha nem um fiscal do Ibama perguntando o que eu estava fazendo ali armado.

Só tinha árvore.

Mato.

Pedra.

E o som dos meus próprios passos destruindo qualquer possibilidade de encontrar um animal em um raio de oito quilômetros.

Eu tentava andar devagar.

Abaixado.

Silencioso.

Mas meu personagem parecia um pedreiro atravessando uma loja de porcelana.

CRACK.

Galho quebrando.

TUM.

Passo pesado.

SHHHHH.

Mato balançando.

Qualquer animal próximo já devia estar avisando os outros:

— “Rapaziada, tem um imbecil armado vindo pela trilha. Vamos mudar de estado.”

Continuei andando.

Mais duas horas.

Aquela altura, eu já não estava mais caçando.

Eu estava fazendo peregrinação.

Meu rifle tinha virado acessório de trilha.

O binóculo era apenas um instrumento para observar árvores mais de perto.

Eu olhava para qualquer movimento no mato e pensava:

— “Agora vai.”

Era uma folha.

— “Ali! Tem alguma coisa!”

Era uma pedra.

Teve uma hora que eu mirei em um arbusto durante quase dois minutos porque jurava que ele estava respirando.

Não estava.

Era só o vento.

Depois de aproximadamente cinco anos civis caminhando pela reserva, finalmente ouvi um barulho diferente.

Passos.

Galhos quebrando.

Alguma coisa se movimentando.

Parei imediatamente.

Meu coração acelerou.

Peguei o binóculo.

E lá estava ele.

Um animal.

Um animal de verdade.

Com pernas.

Corpo.

Vida própria.

Eu quase chorei.

Depois de tantas horas andando, aquele bicho já não era apenas uma presa.

Era uma aparição divina.

Comecei a me aproximar lentamente.

Cada passo era calculado.

Eu tentava controlar a respiração.

Ajustava a posição.

Observava o vento.

Media a distância.

Na minha cabeça, eu estava realizando uma operação de precisão digna de um documentário militar.

Na realidade, eu estava agachado atrás de um arbusto, apertando todos os botões do teclado e tentando descobrir como estabilizava a mira.

O animal ficou parado.

Era a oportunidade perfeita.

Levantei o rifle.

Mirei.

A arma começou a balançar como se meu personagem tivesse tomado sete energéticos e estivesse sendo atacado por ansiedade.

A mira passava pela cabeça.

Pelo pescoço.

Pela perna.

Pela árvore.

Pelo céu.

Menos pelo lugar onde eu queria atirar.

Prendi a respiração.

Tentei alinhar.

O animal começou a se mexer.

Entrei em pânico.

DISPAREI.

BANG.

Acertei.

Eu sabia que tinha acertado porque o animal saiu correndo como se tivesse lembrado que deixou o forno ligado.

Minha reação foi imediata:

— “PEGUEI!”

Não tinha pegado.

Tinha apenas iniciado uma investigação criminal.

Fui até o local do disparo.

Encontrei sangue.

O jogo indicava que o animal estava ferido.

Agora era só seguir o rastro.

Simples.

Pelo menos foi o que eu pensei antes de começar a maior perseguição terrestre desde a invenção do boleto.

Segui a primeira mancha de sangue.

Depois outra.

Mais uma.

O animal continuava correndo.

Cem metros.

Duzentos metros.

Trezentos metros.

Quatrocentos metros.

Eu acompanhando pequenas gotas de sangue no chão como um detetive completamente despreparado.

Toda vez que encontrava uma nova mancha, recuperava a esperança.

— “Agora ele está perto.”

Não estava.

Mais cinquenta metros.

Outra mancha.

— “Agora ele cai.”

Não caiu.

Mais cem metros.

Nesse ponto, eu já estava começando a admirar o animal.

O bicho tinha levado um tiro, perdido sangue por meio quilômetro e continuava correndo com mais disposição do que eu tenho para levantar da cama numa segunda-feira.

A perseguição passou dos quinhentos metros.

Eu entrava no mato.

Saía do mato.

Subia morro.

Descia morro.

Atravessava clareira.

Olhava pegada.

Olhava sangue.

Olhava cocô.

Não sabia mais o que estava seguindo.

Até que o rastro simplesmente desapareceu.

Nada.

Sem sangue.

Sem pegada.

Sem animal.

Ele evaporou.

Fiquei parado no meio da floresta, segurando o rifle, tentando entender como um bicho baleado conseguiu desaparecer com mais eficiência que prestador de serviço depois de receber adiantamento.

Procurei ao redor.

Voltei alguns metros.

Andei em círculos.

Entrei no mato novamente.

Nada.

O animal havia vencido.

Depois de horas caminhando, encontrei uma única presa, acertei um único tiro e ainda assim consegui perder o bicho.

Aceitei a derrota.

Segui minha vida.

Continuei explorando a reserva, fingindo que aquilo fazia parte do plano.

Muito tempo depois, eu estava em outro lugar completamente diferente.

Calmo.

Observando a paisagem.

Quando vi um animal passando ao longe.

Peguei o binóculo.

Dessa vez eu não queria errar.

Observei com atenção.

O animal estava andando devagar.

Muito devagar.

Parecia cansado.

Cambaleava de um lado para o outro.

Eu pensei:

— “Que estranho. Esse bicho está com algum problema.”

Continuei olhando.

Ele deu mais alguns passos.

Parou.

E simplesmente caiu morto.

Do nada.

Fiquei alguns segundos em silêncio.

Meu cérebro tentando processar o que tinha acabado de acontecer.

Aproximei-me.

Analisei o animal.

E então veio a revelação.

Era ele.

O mesmo animal.

O desgraçado que eu tinha acertado horas antes.

O mesmo que correu quinhentos metros sangrando.

O mesmo que desapareceu no meio da floresta.

Ele não tinha escapado.

Ele apenas decidiu morrer no horário dele.

Meu disparo não matou o animal.

Abriu uma solicitação de falecimento com prazo de processamento de três a cinco horas úteis.

Eu efetuei o tiro hoje e a confirmação só chegou depois.

O animal atravessou metade do mapa, resolveu assuntos pessoais, se despediu da família, organizou os documentos e só então falou:

— “Agora eu posso morrer.”

TheHunter: Call of the Wild não é um jogo de caça.

É um simulador de paciência administrativa.

Você anda durante horas.

Não encontra nada.

Quando encontra, não consegue mirar.

Quando consegue mirar, o animal foge.

Quando você segue o animal, perde o rastro.

E quando finalmente desiste, ele aparece morto em outro bairro.

O jogo não recompensa precisão.

Ele recompensa quem tem tempo livre e estabilidade emocional.

Conclusão:

Entrei achando que seria um caçador lendário.

Virei um andarilho armado com problemas de percepção.

Aprendi que os animais escutam absolutamente tudo.

Aprendi que minha mira tem a estabilidade de uma cadeira de plástico quebrada.

E aprendi que, em TheHunter, até a morte dos animais sofre atraso de entrega.

Mas quando aquele bicho finalmente caiu…

Eu senti orgulho.

Não porque fiz um disparo perfeito.

Mas porque, depois de horas, o jogo finalmente confirmou que eu tinha acertado alguma coisa.

E então voltei para a floresta.

Porque aparentemente caminhar durante seis horas para dar um único tiro virou meu novo conceito de diversão.

Czolgasz się przez las do zwierzyny. Sarna jest tylko 100 metrów od Ciebie, ale przez kochane drzewa i wzniesienia to możesz co najwyżej usłyszeć jak ostrzega, że zaraz zrobi teleport na drugą stronę mapy.

A więc czołgaj się przyjacielu, metr zrobisz w 15-20 sekund, matematykę zostawiam Tobie. Udało Ci się dostać na pozycję strzelecką? Gratulacje! Oddaj ten strzał, bo jeśli sarenka się ruszy lub spudlujesz, to czeka Cię festiwal gonienia po lesie.

Teraz zamieniasz się w drapieżnika, poczułeś krew i po jej śladach idziesz. Ale nie tylko, bo ofiarą zostawia jeszcze ślady kopyt i módl się, żeby czasem nie zgłupiała przez drzewa bo ślady bedą tworzyć pentagram, a Ty się będziesz kręcić jak Denzel.

No i najważniejsze. Jesteś taki straszny, że taka srarna to robi pod siebie częściej niż krwawi, więc po kilku godzinach to z tych stolców zwierząt będziesz znał nie tylko kierunek, ale i ich znak zodiaku (no chyba, że zgubisz trop to wtedy, to nie). 

Jak wygladają pierwsze godziny? Tropisz czołgając się godzinę w krzaku, licząc że w tym czasie idziesz w dobrym kierunku, bo przecież jeleń nie będzie czekał całego dnia. Strzelasz i znając życie gonisz go przez krzaczory, zza których widać więcej krzaków. Gdy mija 20 minut okazuje się, że zgubileś trop i w okół jest 5 tysięcy sladów innych łosi, borduków i jenotów. Jak masz jako tako ot entacje w terenie, to wracasz do ostatniego znanego Ci śladu i potem szukasz godzinę teuchła, które gdzieś przepadło (pewnie leży w jednym z miliona krzaków koło Ciebie).

No i bonus. Nie myśl sobie, że jesteś drapieżnikiem alfa. Na Ciebie też może coś zapolować. Na moim przykładzie, jak tylko dorwałem drugi raz jelenia i go trafiłem to nie wiadomo skąd wyskoczyło na mnie stado danieli. 

To nie niedźwiedzie, to wilki czy dziki aą niebezpieczne. A właśnie zwykle daniele, które wyskakują znienacka jak stado dresów i okłada Cię kopytami, aż padniesz. Póki co jedyny raz wpierdziel o skoczyłem tylko od tych niepozornych rogaczy, dlatego potem wracałem w to miejsce z obozu kolejne 40 minut, żeby kolejne 40 szukać tego postrzelonego jelenia.

I am very wary of any game with a library of DLCs as a potential money grabbing scheme. I got this one for just over $1 on sale added a hunting dog DLC, a quad bike DLC, a tent DLC, modern rifles DLC and the Silver Ridge Peaks DLC for a total cost of around $6. The salami slicing of the DLC money grabbing strategy is very obvious even on sale and the $1 for the base game is an obvious “hook”.

The base rifles in the core game are weak and even with a 90% hit rate only yielded about 20% vital organs hits required for a kill. The quad bike is so noisy its mostly useless. The hunting dog DLC has a single dog in it, and you must purchase another if you want another dog. The dog biscuits cost in game, $4000 per 25 pack at a cost of IG$160 per biscuit, while a silver rated kill will yield IG$ of $800 to $1000 on average which means the dog will never get biscuits, simply to expensive. You need the IG money for ammo (IG$700-IG$1000 for 10 rounds of mid-range ammo). 

Only 10 spaces for trophy animals saves so buy another DLC for trophies or delete the lower rated potential trophies (I delete all but the best silver or higher). You seldom have money for taxidermy in any case. 

Your noise level on walking is extremely high, jogging is almost the same noise level as a quad bike, stalking is still noisy and only leopard crawling is silent. Binoculars are weaker than reading glasses. I can see animals with my naked eye and when looking through the binoculars, looking the animal in the eye, still cannot “spot” the animal to mark it for a shot. Marking an animal lasts only about 2 seconds. Animals flee at the slightest noise, or sight, or smell and tracking them is useless as they will run or trot while you will spook them using anything other than leopard crawling. Crawling is slower than leopard crawling. So, the best way to get kills is to jog until you get the odd stalking opportunity or just hit them in the run in a “gun and run” strategy which is absurd for a hunting game. Males are mostly hidden behind females, so you spook the females before you get a shot at a male for trophy animals. Else you just collect low score female kills. Stalking an animal could easily waste up to an hour in real time so it’s only worth doing for real good-looking trophy or “medal” animals. Ambushing is an even bigger waste of time you could sit in ambush for hours without any animal showing up at a designated and timed spot and, more often than not, only females will pitch. You also need expensive bait and lures to make this work and another few DLCs to expand that feature. There is no bait in the base game so you must buy a bait/feeder DLC for that kind of ambush. Water holes are better once you have the drinking spots marked.
      
Want better odds, buy more DLCs

You only get around 8 animals to hunt per reserve and hunting level one animals are often a negative cost game. Shoot them with arrows sometimes work. I leopard crawled into a rafter of turkeys at night with the basic bow and slaughtered them but then a bear and a moose spawned in the same space forcing me to use the handgun and chasing off the turkeys, a cheap strategy. 

Often, missions are absurd asking for animal hunts in areas where the animal is extremely scarce or sanitised for the mission. They like asking for coyote kills and then disappear all the coyotes wasting hours of your time searching for an opportunity, hiding them away just out of reach or just behind the next map contour, rock or tree. The coyote missions are absolutely designed to waste endless time. Then there is also the 2 meters teleport of a targeted animal as you line up a shot. With only 8 animals to hunt, missions are very similar and repetitive or silly like taking photos or searching for lost stuff in a hunting game. The missions soon become absurd given the limitations of the core game. Leopard crawl under the belly of a bull moose and shoot out the left testicle with an ash bow and traditional arrows. I exaggerate but not by much, kill two coyotes, at night with a legal kill around Lake Leviathan is a sample. Missions would also be much easier if you would just buy a few more DLCs for better equipment, or feeders, or bait, or better lures.

Then there are the animal specialities. See an animal through the binoculars, “spot” them and they start running immediately. Mission animals suddenly become immortal especially moose cows. Animals almost always hiding behind trees, rocks or in the dip. Moose or bears spawning where you aim to hunt mission animals to attack you in designated “need” spaces for the mission animals.

Changes in one reserve to the next reserve are mostly skin changes with the base formula remaining mostly the same thus the experience does not change materially from one reserve to another. Bison = Moose, Black Bear = Wild boar, Turkey = Pheasant, etc. 

The Hunter, Call of the Wild has a few moments and is fun sometimes, but the overall experience is very disappointing. The time wasting and the annoying elements eat away at the gaming value but in the end the extreme limitations in the core game and game thesis (hunting for the sake of trophies) is a failure. It is soon boring, a grind to get better hunter stats, upgrade equipment locked behind massive tedious progression requirements, purposeless missions and a hunting experience at a snail’s pace. There is none of the excitement of real life hunting, only tedious canned hunting at its worst. I really tried to get with the game. I've got 156 harvests, 12 gold, 53 silver, 42 bronze and 384m as longest shot. I will not finish the game, there simply is no advanture left, and not much to start off with. I will certainly not be buying any other DLCs.

Review: theHunter: Call of the Wild

A superb hunting simulator that gets nearly everything right — graphics, sound, weapons, animal behavior, tracking, and stalking.

This Is a Hunting Sim, Not a Shooting Sim

Let's set expectations right away: this is not an action game. It's a true hunting and stalking simulator, and it absolutely nails that experience. The Dolby Atmos soundscape is phenomenal, dropping you into the middle of a vibrant wilderness biome full of dynamic animals going about their day.

That means you'll spend a LOT of time traveling between hunting locations and slowly, methodically stalking your prey. Success comes from learning animal trails and paths, and understanding how those affect where animals will be at certain times of day. Wander in the wrong direction and you can easily go 30 minutes of real time without seeing a single track — and each map has its own quirks and randomness that keep things interesting.

The Real Game Is in the Details

What this game rewards most is attention to the meta-details:

What line connects the earliest and longest tracks on your display?
Can you anticipate where an animal is headed based on its speed and direction?
Can you close the distance to land a gold or diamond-rated shot?
And the fun question: which trophies will you mount in your lodge?
Gear Matters (and So Does the DLC)

Like a lot of games these days, the devil is in the DLC. If you want the best experience, plan on picking up several of the DLC weapons, gear packs, and map locations. Each adds custom storylines to complete (which means more XP), and you'll want good gear to progress through them smoothly.

There's nothing worse than finally finding your target and realizing your loadout can't get the job done — and yes, hunting rabbits with 10-gauge slugs is a bit of overkill in the other direction.

The Wild Bites Back

Make no mistake, there are real dangers out there. I've been knocked down or killed by wolf packs, stampeding bison, and rampaging boar. Once enraged, these animals are tougher to drop — they'll charge, pursue, and attack, and trying to land a headshot while dancing around trees to avoid getting trampled is no easy task.

My advice: go the silent route with a bow when you can. But that won't save you from wolf packs. For those, you'll want a big shotgun or a .45 revolver — and a bit of luck. Wolves show up in groups of 2 to 8, and even three is a serious threat.

The good news: their combat AI isn't great. They're slow to pounce because they have to trace a path to you through the terrain, so you can kite them fairly easily. Landing a clean heart shot while doing it, though? Not easy. I've died to three separate packs, but I also managed to take down a complete pack of five with 10-gauge steel birdshot. I knew if I stopped to switch ammo they'd overwhelm me, so I kited and kept shooting — after 2–3 solid hits each, they started dropping. I swear the big one soaked three .45 rounds to the shoulders, a 600-grain arrow to the side, and two loads of birdshot before he finally went down. Sadly, only two of the five ended up trophy-worthy; the rest took too much ammo, and I just started aiming for the head. The shotgun will definitely stun them, at least.

Progression: Slow but Rewarding

Leveling feels a tad slow, but every level unlocks a skill or perk that meaningfully improves stealth or accuracy — the core of the game. The XP system rewards careful, quality play: a single hard-difficulty trophy harvest is worth more than gunning down a whole herd of trivial roe deer. You can do that if the opportunity presents itself, but it's largely not worth your time. One big old moose will net you more XP than a pile of easy kills.

Verdict

If you want instant action, look elsewhere. But if the idea of reading tracks, playing the wind, and earning that perfect diamond harvest appeals to you, theHunter: Call of the Wild is one of the best in the genre.

The game has some merit but honestly it runs short of its price tag and is just not enough for me to get into it seriously. The game systems are a bit wooden and it's very non-intuitive for beginners. You have to watch guides and videos to get how things work and farm for dozens of hours before you have skills that make it a bit more decent in terms of quality of life. And unfortunately, at that point - there's nothing else to it. You just keep doing the same thing but more proficiently and you're supposed to be excited about rare spawns and chase them but... That's just not enough of a foundation to stay engaged with this.

The asking price is a bit much for a one dimensional game and unfortunately, on that front it gets much much worse - a LOT of the content is behind a paywall and they've gone absolutely crazy on DLCs. It's too much, every little thing that would compliment your experience of the game is paid separately when it should have been included - since the game doesn't have enough variety and content to stand on its own, this is not an extra - it's part of the experience and should be in the base game. It's wildly financially irresponsible to spend money that way and besides a few people who have found something in this game to make it their passion, I don't see why someone would buy up  two dozen DLCs just to try and experience some fun with a product which they have bought as well. 

To sum it up - it's just not worth the price and the practice of releasing small, incremental upgrades and pay walling each one separately is extremely shady in my eyes. I am not a cash cow for you, I just wanted to try out your product and honestly, while I had a bit of fun, I got the hang of the game and its flow and it just can't keep me - there's not enough there. I think I bought this quite discounted years ago but full price - simply cannot recommend. The content does not justify the asking price and when you consider the DLC practice... should not be encouraged.

是個需要慢慢花時間上手的遊戲，尤其對那些來自沒有狩獵文化的國家的人而言，這個遊戲並不算是爽Game，而是需要慢慢學習知識、探索的遊戲，所以對新玩家而言剛開始會很受挫，但慢慢的理解之後狩獵就沒那麼困難了。
剛開始玩的20個小時左右花了很多時間認識這個遊戲，好幾個晚上玩了很久也沒打到任何獵物，完全是走路模擬器的狀態，但後面理解各種機制之後，就覺得簡單多了，只是要花很多時間農等級解開武器技能點。
整體而言遊戲很寫實，和朋友一起狩獵的話，誰先開槍獵物就會逃亡，越野機車跟狗都會把獵物嚇跑，走路穿越灌木叢也是，唯一不寫實的大概就只有傳送而已。
有個重點一定要記得，下線前記得把便攜式的東西收好，我為了狩獵郊狼而買的高腳椅已經不知道消失在育空的哪裡了...系統已經說弄丟了。
跟朋友一起邊聊天邊狩獵應該很有趣吧，不過有點難找到喜歡這種慢步調寫實遊戲的朋友哈哈。

Це найкраща гра про полювання з дуже класним візуалом, атмосферою та приємною стрільбою.
Але чи рекомендував би я її? Більше ні аніж так. Проблема полягає в жадібності розробників, які зробили красиву гру, але пусту в середині, а для того щоб це виправити - купуй ДЛС.

• Різноманіття зброї тут жахливе. Гравцю по дефолту дають 2 гвинтівки які без ДЛС у вас не буде чим замінити, бо всі інші дві з половиною гвинтівки які тут є, банально гірші. Схожа ситуація і з револьверами, а дробовиків у грі лише два, один із яких дають безкоштовно.

• Карт у грі без ДЛС всього дві. Але тут притензія не скільки до кількості карт, а до їх якості. Карти в цій грі невиправдано гіганські. На них нічого цікавого, це просто ліс, поляни та гори, на яких бігає всього по 8-9 тварин, і більшу частину часу ви буде зустрічати лише меншу половину із них. На картах розкидані точки обзору та бази з магазином і вам їх потрібно відкривати, а через маштаби карти, у вас це буде займати неймовірну кількість часу та нервів.

• Баги. Постійно зустрічаються випадки коли тварини застряють в кущах, або ходять на задніх лапах, або взагалі намертво встають і перестають реагувати на гравця. І це не поодинокі випадки, тварини постійно смикаються, підпригують, забігають під воду і все в такому роді.

• Щодо самих ДЛС, то їх якість жахлива. Карти пусті і гіганські, а зброю продають всього по 3 штуки в одному ДЛС, і в більшості випадків це схожі модельки, анімації, навіть звук з мінімальними змінами, через це вся зброя у грі відчуваєтсья ідентично. Крім того, купуючи ДЛС на зброю, вона видаєтсья вам безкоштовно, тобто придбавши ДЛС у вас вже буде найкраща зброя у грі, замін якій не має. Який тоді сенс грати у цю гру? Трофеї??

• Трофеї. У безкоштовний будик де можна розміщувати ваші трофеї, ніхто крім вас зайти не може. Щоб демонструвати іншим людям тварин яких ви вполювали, вам необхідно купити ДЛС з іншим будинком. І ніби цього було мало, так ще в дефолтному будинку ви не зможете розміщувати тварин із ДЛС карт.

[h2]Підсумок[/h2]
Ця гра має красиву обготку і якщо вам цікаво зайти на годин п'ять постріляти і вийти, то для вас гра буде чудовим віріантом навіть без ДЛС. Але якщо ви розраховуєте грати довше, то готуйтесь платити... і навіть якщо ви будете платити, це не змінить проблеми з відсутністю зброї, багами, та одноманітними, нудними і надто гіганськими картами.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)
theHunter: Call of the Wild is, hands down, a great game. It nails the essence of real-world hunting better than almost anything else on the market.
The attention to detail in the animal designs, behaviors, and massive open-world maps is breathtaking. From dense forests to sprawling plains, every reserve feels alive. Even better, the developers actually support the game with genuinely good updates—frequently remastering animal models, upgrading textures, and improving graphics so the game continues to look amazing over time.
What really sets this game apart, though, is the core gameplay loop: it doesn't give away easy wins. If you want to bag a massive trophy animal, you have to earn it. It can take hours of tracking, observing wind direction, managing your noise, and waiting for the perfect shot.
Just like real hunting, this game demands genuine patience, stealth, and strategic planning. That slow-burn build-up makes landing a clean shot on a rare animal feel incredibly satisfying.

Seit 2018 dabei und immer wieder jedes Jahr aufs neue komm Ich zurück einfach um die Landschaft zu genießen ^^ aber vorallem wegen der unfassbar dichten Atmosphäre.

Es gibt einfach kaum ein anderes Spiel, bei dem man so gut abschalten kann. Man streift stundenlang durch die endlosen, wunderschönen Reviere (Hirschfelden im Herbst ist nach wie vor ein Traum!), hört nur den Wind in den Bäumen und das Knacken der eigenen Schritte. Es ist pure Entspannung – bis man plötzlich einen Warnruf hört oder eine frische Fährte im Boden entdeckt. Dann schlägt das Ganze sofort in puren Nervenkitzel um.

Das Spiel erfordert viel Geduld und ist kein schnelles Arcade-Geballer. Man muss das Verhalten der Tiere lernen, auf den Wind achten und sich ruhig verhalten. Aber genau diese Lernkurve und die Geduld machen jeden erfolgreichen Schuss am Ende umso belohnender.

Was Call of the Wild auch nach all den Jahren noch so besonders macht:

    Die Grafik: Auch Jahre nach Release sehen die Wälder, Lichtstimmungen und Tiere fantastisch aus.

    Das Sounddesign: Absolute Spitzenklasse. Egal ob Regen, Tierlaute oder das Rascheln im Gebüsch – es zieht einen sofort ins Spiel.

    Der Umfang: Es gibt mittlerweile so viele verschiedene Karten und Tierarten, dass es nie langweilig wird.

Für mich ein absoluter Dauerbrenner auf der Festplatte, der nie deinstalliert wird. Wer Natur, ein bisschen Taktik und Geduld mitbringt, wird hier hunderte Stunden versenken können. Klare Kaufempfehlung! 🌲🦌

theHunter: Call of the Wild é muito mais que um jogo de caça — é um simulador de paciência, observação e imersão. Os gráficos são deslumbrantes, com florestas, sons e sensação de presença que fazem você se sentir realmente na natureza. Caçar exige rastrear pegadas, checar o vento, escolher a arma certa e calcular o tiro com cuidado; se fizer barulho ou errar, o animal foge. A sensação de passar horas seguindo um rastro e finalmente acertar o disparo perfeito é incomparável. É relaxante, imersivo e viciante do jeito bom.
Mas não é pra todo mundo. É lento: andar quilômetros devagar, perder o rastro, assustar o bicho sem querer e errar o tiro fazem parte. Quem tem pouca paciência vai se frustrar. E o pior: o jogo é infestado de DLCs — armas, mapas, equipamentos... parece que até pra algumas coisas básicas você precisa pagar a mais. Tem também relatos de tiros em órgãos vitais que não contam e troféus perdidos por bugs. Sem as DLCs, a experiência fica bem limitada.
Resumindo: se você gosta de calma, observação e imersão, é uma obra-prima. Se busca ação rápida e tiros certeiros, vai achar chato. Compre o jogo base com calma e só depois veja se vale a pena investir nas DLCs. E lembre-se: a caça exige tempo, silêncio e perseverança. 🦌🎯

If you’re not someone who has several hours to play continuously in one sitting, I really don’t think this game is a good fit for you. I bought this game during a sale, so I already came into it with pretty low expectations. I wasn't expecting a perfect game, and I was willing to overlook quite a few things.

The hunting itself is fun, and the maps are beautiful. There is definitely a good game underneath all of this. Unfortunately, the overall user experience is much more frustrating than it needs to be.

The controls and UI are unnecessarily confusing. There are so many menus, functions, key bindings and systems that it’s often difficult to figure out where something is or how to do something. I ended up having to search YouTube for tutorials just to understand basic operations. And there are *a lot* of tutorials explaining these basic things. To me, that says something about the design: if players constantly need external videos to understand the fundamentals, the UI and controls probably weren't designed clearly enough.

The way saving and progression work is also very frustrating. You can only properly restart from an Outpost, so if you stop playing in the middle of a mission, you may have to walk all the way back to where you were when you return. I was willing to tolerate that.

But then the game crashed.

After restarting, my position wasn't saved, so I was sent back to the Outpost and had to walk for another ten-plus minutes just to get back to where I had been before the crash. All that time was simply wasted.

I understand that this is a game about exploration and hunting, and I don't expect everything to be instant. But when basic systems make you repeatedly spend a significant amount of time simply retracing your steps, it becomes very frustrating—especially for players who can only play in shorter sessions.

The developers seem very eager to keep releasing DLCs and monetizing the game, but I really think some of that effort should go toward improving the **basic systems, UI, controls, saving, and overall quality of life first.
