Me encanta este juego.

Eso es lo que hace esto mucho peor.

Llevo 110 horas jugando a *theHunter: Call of the Wild*. He recorrido sus bosques, sus montañas, sus pantanos. He aprendido a leer huellas, a seguir rastros, a escuchar el viento y a distinguir los sonidos de los animales.

He aprendido a cazar.

Y en esas 110 horas he llegado a comprender una verdad que ningún tutorial tuvo la decencia de explicarme:

**Los coyotes son una aberración.**

No los odio porque sean fuertes.

No los odio porque sean peligrosos.

No los odio porque sean difíciles de matar.

Los odio porque son cobardes.

Cobardes de una manera tan absurda que parece que el juego entero fue diseñado para permitirles escapar de mí.

He visto ciervos quedarse quietos.

He visto osos.

He visto animales que deberían tener motivos perfectamente razonables para huir de un hombre armado.

Pero un coyote escucha mi respiración.

Un coyote escucha mis pasos.

Un coyote probablemente escucha mis pensamientos.

Y corre.

Corre antes de que yo pueda verlo.

Corre antes de que yo pueda apuntar.

Corre antes de que yo siquiera sepa que estaba ahí.

Y entonces empieza.

La persecución.

La huella.

La otra huella.

El excremento.

La llamada.

Otra huella.

Un sonido a lo lejos.

Me agacho.

Avanzo.

Espero.

Escucho.

Nada.

Entonces lo encuentro.

A kilómetros de distancia.

Y cuando finalmente consigo una línea de tiro...

**huye.**

He visto desaparecer coyotes detrás de colinas.

He visto coyotes cruzar bosques enteros.

He visto coyotes convertir una caminata relajante en una operación militar de cuarenta minutos.

Y cada vez que uno huye pienso lo mismo:

¿Por qué?

¿Por qué eres así?

¿Qué te hice?

Yo solo quería cazarte.

No era personal.

Ahora lo es.

Porque puedo perdonar que un animal me detecte.

Puedo perdonar que huya.

Puedo perdonar incluso que falle un disparo.

Pero no puedo perdonar que un coyote aparezca después de veinte minutos de rastreo, se encuentre conmigo a una distancia perfectamente razonable y decida que la mejor respuesta posible es **desaparecer del mapa**.

He aprendido a odiar los sonidos.

He aprendido a odiar los bosques.

He aprendido a odiar cada pequeña rama que cruje bajo mis pies porque sé que, en algún lugar, un coyote ya está corriendo.

Y lo más terrible es que el juego no me obliga a hacer esto.

Podría ignorarlos.

Podría cazar otra cosa.

Podría simplemente disfrutar del paisaje.

Pero sé que están ahí.

Sé que existen.

Sé que en algún lugar de ese bosque hay uno.

Uno que todavía no he visto.

Uno que todavía no me ha escuchado.

Uno que todavía no ha cometido el error de cruzarse conmigo.

Y entonces recuerdo las 110 horas.

Las 110 horas de huellas.

De rastros.

De llamadas.

De carreras.

De disparos fallidos.

De coyotes que escaparon.

Y comprendo que esto ya no es cacería.

Es memoria.

Es acumulación.

Es rencor.

Porque yo puedo cerrar el juego.

Puedo apagar el monitor.

Puedo levantarme de la silla.

Pero ellos siguen ahí.

En algún servidor.

En algún bosque.

Corriendo.

Esperando.

Huyendo de mí antes de que siquiera llegue.

Y eso es lo que más odio.

Que no puedo hacer nada para que tengan miedo de mí.

Porque ya tienen miedo.

**Tienen demasiado miedo.**

Y quiero que sepan que los odio.

Quiero que cada coyote de cada reserva, cada coyote que haya existido y cada coyote que todavía no haya generado el juego, conozca mi odio.

Quiero que cada uno de sus pequeños corazones digitales comprenda las 110 horas que llevo acumulando esto.

Si pudiera escribir mi odio hacia los coyotes en cada árbol de cada reserva, no habría suficientes árboles.

Si pudiera escribirlo en cada piedra, no habría suficientes piedras.

Si pudiera escribirlo en cada huella que han dejado, tendría que perseguirlos hasta el fin del mapa.

Y todavía no sería suficiente.

Porque no quiero que dejen de existir.

No.

Eso sería demasiado sencillo.

Quiero que existan.

Quiero que sigan apareciendo.

Quiero que sigan corriendo.

Quiero seguir encontrándolos.

Quiero que cada vez que escuche ese maldito aullido, sepa exactamente lo que significa.

Que estoy aquí.

Que tengo un rifle.

Que tengo paciencia.

Y que, algún día, algún coyote se va a quedar quieto el tiempo suficiente.

Ese día no habrá huella.

No habrá persecución.

No habrá distancia.

Solo habrá un disparo.

Y entonces volveré a caminar tranquilamente por el bosque.

Porque amo este juego.

Es relajante.

Es divertido.

Es práctico.

Es suficientemente realista para sentirse vivo y suficientemente videojuego para no convertirse en un simulador de burocracia forestal.

Es, en general, un juego excelente.

**Pero odio a los coyotes.**

Los odio.

Los odio.

Los odio.

Y después de 110 horas...

I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME!! I am 160 hours in and still not bored of this game!I have been playing for a few years now, first on Xbox and now on Steam. I own all of the map DLCs as well as a few others so I have TONS to do. I love that it does come with quite a bit to do in the base game alone though!!  There are some bugs here and there, but what game doesn't have bugs? 
I am the kind of person that favors nature, and this game delivers! Half the time I am running around adoring the views around me (in game photo option comes in handy). The graphics are amazing, even before upgrading my PC it was beautiful, but even more so now. The animal fur, the trees, the sunsets, the mountains, the textures, it is all amazing in my opinion. Even the sounds of the outdoors is so calming.
As for the entire point of the game- I have a LOT of fun playing this game for the hunting as well. I personally have never been hunting, but I do enjoy playing the part with this game. I understand where others feel it is not perfect, but for me it is great! I don't really go out of my way to get high tier animals/great ones, or make a whole steak-out spot, but thankfully you don't HAVE to do that. I just like to find "unique" fur patterns and what not, and stack up money for better items, which is still just as fun for me. PLUS you can put your most prized animal trophies up in a trophy lodge and there is a lot to do with that!!
All in all-this game is perfect for those who have no idea how to hunt or who love to hunt, perfect for those who adore wildlife and scenery, and perfect for me. It could still use some work with the bugs, and making it more "realistic" for those who are pro hunters and might be a bit more nitpicky, but honestly the game itself is amazing. There is tons to do, especially with in-game missions on each map to help you get money, level up, and gain experience. Happy hunting!!!

theHunter: Call of the Wild is probably one of the better hunting simulators out there, but unfortunately it isn't for me.

The game can feel surprisingly realistic at times. Animals behave differently, tracking them requires patience and choosing the right weapon and ammunition matters. The environments also look great, and the huge maps create a convincing wilderness atmosphere.

The problem is that I don't find the actual gameplay particularly enjoyable. A lot of the time you're either waiting for an animal to appear from a hunting spot or running across a huge map from one mission objective to another. There is a lot of downtime, and I often found myself spending more time walking around than actually hunting. Especially hunting deer can feel like a game of chance, because if you run around near lakes, you're bound to come across deer that don't even notice you.

The shooting mechanics also take some of the enjoyment away for me. The rifle wobbles so much that lining up a shot can become frustrating, especially when you're trying to make a precise shot at a longer distance. I understand that some weapon sway is intended to make hunting more realistic, but in practice I often found it more annoying than immersive. And I'm a hunter in real life, so I know what it feels like to shoot a shotgun or a rifle. If a hunter had such awful wobble, I would revoke their hunting license immediately.

The damage system can also feel inconsistent. Sometimes hitting a vital organ drops an animal quickly, while other shots that look like they should cause catastrophic damage result in only a very low bleed rate. It can make the game feel less like a realistic simulation and more like you're trying to hit specific invisible hit zones.

The maps are enormous, but fast travel points are relatively sparse. There is an ATV, but it's locked behind paid DLC, which I just can't endorse.

Overall, I can understand why theHunter: Call of the Wild has such a dedicated player base, and I can see that a lot of effort has gone into making it a detailed hunting simulator. However, the slow gameplay, excessive walking, weapon sway and sometimes questionable damage system make it difficult for me to enjoy. It may be one of the better hunting simulators available, but it simply isn't a game I find particularly fun to play.

I have been playing this game for years, sinking hours upon hours into this game on the xbox and about 80 since getting into pc gaming. I grew up playing cabellas games on the wii and as a hunter myself I was pumped to see an open world hunting sim. It took a long time to learn the mechanics and understand all the inner workings within the game and I stuck around for it desperately trying to convince myself it was a fun game, but I think I’ve finally reached the point where I can’t keep lying to myself. This game is f*cking boring, the UI is easily the worst I’ve ever seen and have had to use, and everything about it feels so damn lazy. Dangerous animal encounters are the equivalent to watching paint dry. You ready your gun at a snails pace while the animal gets in your general vicinity which lowers a health bar in the corner of your screen. Your players reaction to getting “hit” by an animal is to make a noise and you slide backwards a little. The hunts feel fun initially, getting your first diamond is a rush, getting a rare coloration is fun, but great ones are such a slog. Setting up the grind is fun but actually doing it gets boring very quickly. With such barebones gameplay, finally getting your great one gives you that feeling of “I just sunk hours of my life to get a virtual deer that looks a little cooler than the others”. I get this is some people’s jam and I am not trying to hate on them but I’m tired of hearing them d riding themselves for enjoying the game. When is there going to be a hunting game with some weight behind the encounters. I want dangerous hunts to feel dangerous, where if I get clawed by a bear there is an actual animation for it, or where there might be a better option than just standing still and shooting and hoping it dies or runs away before your green bar of health empties. I want to explore cool maps not these empty expanses that are large just for the sake of being large. I want animal AI to be better than Pac-Man ghosts. I want my hunter to be an actual marksman who can reload at a decent pace and hold a f*cking 6 pound gun steady and handle recoil like anybody that shoots often should be able to (the skills to improve this are laughably useless). I know this is a rant and I may be going over the top with the complaining but I desperately wanted this game to give me those Cabellas dangerous hunt feelings but with mechanics built in to keep it up to date and fresh. If you are a hunter that wants to pass some time with a game catered to your hobby you oughta wait for something better. Actually going out to hunt brings food to the table and sometimes an awesome trophy to show off to the boys, the hunts in this game offer no gratification and genuinely feel like a waste of time.

With 100 hours played and Level 30 reached, I think I've spent enough time with theHunter: Call of the Wild to say that this is a game I genuinely keep coming back to.

In fact, this is one of those games where, on my gaming days, I sometimes find myself starting it right at the beginning of the day. There is just something incredibly relaxing and satisfying about stepping into the wilderness and deciding for yourself what kind of day you're going to have.

What I particularly appreciate is that you don't need a dog or additional content to enjoy the game properly. The base experience stands on its own extremely well. You can explore, hunt, track animals, discover new areas, and simply enjoy being out there without feeling like you're missing something essential.

The tent system is another feature I really love. Being able to place your own tents and create personal starting points around the maps gives you a surprising amount of freedom. Over time, you end up creating your own little network of hunting spots, and that makes each map feel much more personal.

And speaking of the maps: they are outstanding. The environments are beautifully designed, varied, and incredibly immersive. Whether you're slowly moving through dense forests, crossing open landscapes, or simply sitting somewhere and watching the world around you, the maps do a fantastic job of making you feel like you're actually there.

I'm also playing on Linux, and I'm genuinely impressed with how well the game runs for me. Performance is very good, and the shaders load exceptionally fast on my system. So far, theHunter: Call of the Wild has been one of the games that has surprised me the most in that regard.

100 hours in, Level 30, and I'm still coming back to it.

That's probably the best recommendation I can give.

購入を迷っている方に一言で言うなら、**「まったり狩猟を楽しみたいなら買って損はない。ただし序盤はキツい」**です。

このゲームはスキルやパークがあり、狩猟を重ねるほど自分が強くなっていきます。一方で、動物側が成長して強くなるようなシステムではありません。つまり、一番大変なのはゲームを始めた直後です。

特に序盤は、動物を見つけること自体が難しく、私も最初は数時間ひたすら歩き回るだけで「何をすればいいんだ……」となり、すぐにやめてしまいました。

その後、友人とマルチプレイをする機会があり、いろいろ教えてもらったことで徐々に狩れるようになりました。スキルも重要ですが、プレイヤー自身の経験もかなり重要なゲームだと思います。


DLCは必須ではありません。DLCなしでも全クラスの動物を狩ることはできます。

ただし、狩猟効率はDLCがあるとかなり変わります。

特に強力な武器を序盤から使えるようになるのは大きなメリットです。「最初から強い武器を持ったら飽きるのでは？」と思うかもしれませんが、このゲームは誰かと競うゲームではありません。

楽に狩れるなら、それでいい。狩猟を楽しむことが目的です。

DLCなしの場合、強力な武器を入手するためにゲーム内のお金や武器経験値を貯める必要があります。せっかく強い武器が欲しくなったタイミングで、さらに経験値稼ぎが必要になるのは結構大変です。

初めてDLCを買うなら

いきなり大量のDLCを買うのが不安な方には、個人的には以下がおすすめです。

狩猟犬
撃った獲物を追跡するのに便利。
序盤は追跡スキルもなく、撃った動物を見失いやすいため特に助かります。
Weapon Pack 2
追加武器がどれも序盤から使いやすい。
一通りいろいろな武器を使ってみたい人向け。
これ一つでクラス1～9まで対応できます。
High Caliber Weapon Pack
特に高クラスの動物を狩りやすくなります。
低クラスなら初期ライフルのレンジャーでも十分なので、高クラス狩猟を重視する人向け。

最後に個人的におすすめの武器

■ ライフル

アルジナ .300タクティカルマグナム
クラス7～9を狩るなら非常に優秀。高ランク狩猟の難易度がかなり変わります。これ一本あると高クラス狩猟がかなり楽になります。

フロスト .257
中クラス向け。クラス2～6まで幅広く対応できるので使いやすいです。

ヴァイラント .22LR
クラス1専用。鳥などをバードショット以外で狩りたい場合におすすめ。

■ ショットガン

グリェルク・ドリリングライフル
スラッグがまっすぐ飛び、最初からスコープも付いているので狙いやすいです。

■ ハンドガン

.45-70 イェルンベリ・スペリオル
ハンドガンで高クラスを狩るならかなり優秀。クラス4～9に対応。

アンダーソン .22LR
クラス1専用。軽量で連射もでき、スコープも装着可能なので便利。

マンギアフィコ .410/45コルト
火力は控えめですが、バードショットも使用可能。これ一本でクラス1～5まで対応できます。スコープも装着可能。バードショット用のライフルやショットガンを持ちたくない場合に。

総評

序盤は「動物が見つからない」「撃っても仕留められない」「どこに行けばいいのか分からない」と、かなり苦労すると思います。

ただ、スキルを覚え、武器を揃え、プレイヤー自身も狩猟に慣れてくると一気に面白くなります。

「のんびり歩きながら動物を探して、じっくり狩猟を楽しみたい」人にはかなりおすすめ。

もちろん、ニードゾーンを調べ上げてじっくり待つ狩猟も。

逆に、序盤からサクサク狩りたい人には少し厳しいゲームです。

個人的には、最初の数時間を乗り越えられるかどうかが、このゲームを楽しめるかの分かれ目だと思います。

Ich habe das Spiel mittlerweile einige Stunden gespielt und muss sagen, dass ich positiv überrascht bin. Anfangs war ich mir gar nicht sicher, ob mich ein Jagdspiel überhaupt lange beschäftigen kann, aber genau das Gegenteil ist passiert. Man kann hier erstaunlich viel Zeit verbringen, ohne dass es sich ständig nach dem gleichen Ablauf anfühlt.

Besonders gut gefällt mir die offene Welt. Es gibt verschiedene Gebiete, unterschiedliche Tiere und je nachdem, wo man unterwegs ist, muss man seine Vorgehensweise anpassen. Man läuft nicht einfach los und schießt auf alles, was sich bewegt. Man muss Spuren suchen, Geräusche beachten, auf Wind und Entfernung achten und manchmal auch einfach geduldig sein. Gerade das macht für mich einen großen Teil des Reizes aus.

Was mir ebenfalls gefällt, ist die Atmosphäre. Wenn man alleine durch den Wald läuft und plötzlich irgendwo ein Tier hört, aber nicht weiß, wo es ist, kann das schon ziemlich spannend sein. Die Landschaften sind teilweise wirklich schön gemacht und man kann sich einfach mal eine ganze Weile umschauen und herumstreifen, ohne unbedingt ein bestimmtes Ziel zu haben.

Im Multiplayer macht das Spiel meiner Meinung nach nochmal deutlich mehr Spaß. Zusammen mit Freunden durch die Gegend zu laufen, Tiere aufzuspüren und sich gegenseitig zu helfen, funktioniert erstaunlich gut. Manchmal ist man zwar zehn Minuten unterwegs und findet überhaupt nichts, aber genau solche Situationen gehören irgendwie dazu. Und wenn man dann endlich ein gutes Tier findet, ist die Freude umso größer.

Man sollte allerdings wissen, dass das Spiel nicht besonders schnell ist. Wer ein Spiel erwartet, bei dem ständig etwas passiert und man alle paar Minuten Action hat, wird wahrscheinlich schnell gelangweilt sein. Hier geht es eher um Geduld und darum, sich auf die Jagd einzulassen. Teilweise kann es schon etwas nervig sein, wenn man lange einer Spur folgt und am Ende trotzdem nichts findet.

Auch das Freischalten von besserer Ausrüstung dauert seine Zeit. Gerade am Anfang fühlt sich manches etwas langsam an und man muss erstmal einiges an Geld und Erfahrung sammeln. Für mich ist das aber kein wirklicher Kritikpunkt, weil dadurch auch ein gewisser Fortschritt entsteht und man sich über neue Waffen oder Ausrüstung tatsächlich freut.

Was ich besonders gut finde, ist, dass man nicht gezwungen wird, ständig irgendwelche Missionen abzuarbeiten. Man kann einfach selbst entscheiden, was man machen möchte. Mal geht man gezielt auf ein bestimmtes Tier, mal erkundet man ein neues Gebiet und manchmal läuft man einfach irgendwo herum und schaut, was man findet.

Insgesamt ist theHunter: Call of the Wild für mich ein richtig gutes Spiel, wenn man mit der langsamen Spielweise etwas anfangen kann. Es ist kein Spiel für schnelle Action, sondern eher etwas zum Abschalten und gleichzeitig konzentrierten Spielen. Mit Freunden macht es nochmal mehr Spaß und man kann problemlos viele Stunden darin verbringen.

Von mir gibt es eine klare Empfehlung. Man muss sich am Anfang ein bisschen einarbeiten und darf nicht erwarten, dass direkt alles freigeschaltet ist. Wenn man sich darauf einlässt, bekommt man aber eine ziemlich große und abwechslungsreiche Jagdwelt, in der es auch nach vielen Stunden noch genug zu entdecken gibt.

NOT RECOMMENDED

I own theHunter: Call of the Wild, and this negative review isn't because I suddenly think COTW is a terrible game. I mean, it's way more arcade-like than Classic and I personally don't like that at all. Classic always felt much more like an actual hunting simulation to me.

But that's not even the main reason for this review.

Expansive Worlds / Avalanche Studios have completely destroyed my trust in them as a customer.

I supported theHunter Classic for more than 13 years. I put hundreds of hours into it and spent a ridiculous amount of real money on memberships, em$, weapons, equipment, tents and other content. I played it for well over a decade, much of that time with the same friend.

Some of us literally grew older with this game.

And now Classic is being permanently shut down on November 11, 2026. There is no offline mode, no announced option for community-hosted servers and no legacy version. Once the servers are gone, that's it.

What makes this even worse is the timeline.

On March 31, 2026, the producer of theHunter Classic described a major backend upgrade as "absolutely critical for the future of the game" and as the foundation that would allow Classic to keep growing and improving in the long term.

On June 11, players were told that this backend upgrade had reached its final integration stage, that most of the functionality was already working and that development had made good progress.

Sounds pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ alive to me.

On June 12 there was another normal weekly sale with rifles, tripod stands, tents and other items at up to 40% off. More sales followed on June 26.

And on July 3 — just six days before the shutdown announcement — there was yet another regular sale including rifles, tripod rests, tents and other items.

Then on July 9, suddenly the message was that the playerbase was dwindling, continued support was no longer financially sustainable, and Classic would be permanently shut down four months later.

So I have a very simple question:

When exactly was the decision to shut down theHunter Classic made?

Because either that decision happened unbelievably fast, or those sales were still running while a shutdown was already being considered internally.

I don't know which one it was, but I think the community deserves an answer.

If management already knew where this was heading while players were still being told about the game's long-term future and paid content was being promoted, that would be absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disgusting.

And if they genuinely didn't know until shortly before July 9, then I'd love to know how a 17-year-old live-service game went from "keep growing and improving in the long term" to permanent shutdown within a matter of weeks.

To be fair, once the shutdown was officially announced on July 9, they disabled the purchase of new em$.

Good.

The question is what happened before July 9.

And Classic wasn't some tiny charity project they generously kept alive either.

Avalanche Studios themselves stated in June 2015 that, since late 2012, theHunter had grown from 1 million to more than 5 million players, total revenue had doubled every year during that period, and Expansive Worlds had grown from 6 developers to nearly 30.

This was a successful commercial product that helped grow Expansive Worlds. Millions of people played it, and it was monetized for many years.

I don't expect them to keep developing or hosting a 17-year-old game forever. Games get old and servers cost money. I get that.

What pisses me off is that after monetizing Classic for all those years, they're shutting it down without leaving players any meaningful way to keep playing it.

A server shutdown wasn't some unpredictable event nobody could have seen coming. If you operate an online-only game for 17 years, at some point you should probably have an answer to the question:

"What happens when we eventually turn the servers off?"

Maybe an offline mode would have required serious work. Maybe community servers would have required backend changes. Fine. Nobody is pretending this could have been done in five minutes.

But they had years to come up with some kind of end-of-life solution — an offline mode, community servers, a stripped-down legacy version, whatever.

Instead we're left with a shutdown date and nothing but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ screenshots and memories.

And oh boy, that leaves a bitter taste. In hindsight, it makes the whole business model look like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cash grab: take people's money for years, keep selling digital content tied to an online service, then eventually pull the plug and leave paying customers with nothing they can actually keep using.

And before someone says "it's just an old game" — nah, ♥♥♥♥ that.

For a lot of us this wasn't some disposable game we played for a few weeks and forgot about. We spent years in those reserves.

Why does any of this matter in a Call of the Wild review?

Because COTW is another product from Expansive Worlds, and whether I recommend spending time and money on it also depends on whether I trust the company behind it.

I don't anymore.

Seeing how one of their longest-running and heavily monetized games is being handled at the end of its life has completely changed whether I'm willing to recommend another Expansive Worlds game or spend money on its DLC.

"Community" sounds great when you're selling content. This is where you find out how much that word was actually worth.

I will never financially support Expansive Worlds or Avalanche Studios again.

What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame.

There's plenty of species but as a real-life turkey hunter I'm pretty drawn to the turkeys in the game. They behave a bit dumber than real turkeys but they do actually follow a lot of the same patterns. Its ridiculously fun to set up a little blind or hole up in a bush and pop up a decoy or two before sounding off that turkey call. You'll hear the hens putt and the toms gobble and before long they'll be in your lap. Its a really well done mechanic just never gets old for me. You can even stalk up on them in tall grass if you're careful, place a decoy right close to them and get real selective with your tom. Its the only game that's ever even tried to get turkey hunting right to my knowledge and you can tell they did some research. The only thing that makes me chuckle a bit is the fan design on the turkeys. Its just off. The feathers spiral in one direction. Would love to see that patched one day in a similar fashion to the TruRacs fix for the deer antlers.
Anyway, thank you devs for the free copy. I'll probably nab the Del Arroyo and Labrador Retriever DLCs when they go on sale.
